description.es-ES: La historia que Santa Teresa escribió de sus fundaciones, de San José de Ávila a Burgos (1562–1582): los caminos, las casas, las personas, los trabajos y las mercedes del Señor, con avisos de oración para las prioras. Texto crítico del P. Silverio de Santa Teresa, con sus notas.
description.en-US: St. Teresa's account of the foundation of her convents, from St. Joseph's at Ávila to Burgos (1562–1582): the journeys, the houses, the people, the trials and the graces of the Lord, with counsels on prayer for prioresses. English translation by Sister Agnes Mason, with her notes.
description.pt-BR: A história que Santa Teresa escreveu das suas fundações, de São José de Ávila a Burgos (1562–1582): os caminhos, as casas, as pessoas, as provações e as graças do Senhor, com avisos de oração para as prioras.

sources.edition: Obras de Sta. Teresa de Jesús, ed. P. Silverio de Santa Teresa, C.D., t. V: Libro de las Fundaciones (Biblioteca Mística Carmelitana 5), Burgos: El Monte Carmelo, 1918, pp. 1–329. Princeton Theological Seminary scan, primary OCR.
sources.description: Spanish critical text with Silverio's notes kept as footnotes; his introduction and the appendices are not included. OCR of two independent scans merged word by word.
sources.tierEvidence: Teresa died in 1582; the volume was published in 1918 (public domain in the US) and P. Silverio died in 1954, so his notes are public domain under life+70 since 1 January 2025.

sources.edition: The same volume, Wellesley College scan, used as the second witness.

Saint Theresa: the History of her Foundations, translated from the Spanish by Sister Agnes Mason, C.H.F., with a preface by Sir E. M. Satow, Cambridge: at the University Press, 1909. University of Toronto scan.
sources.description: English translation with Mason's footnotes; the preface and the index are not included. Mason follows Teresa's 31 chapters, so the chapter ids match the Spanish. The Lewis/Zimmerman version (1913) was left aside because its OCR is too damaged to split reliably.
sources.tierEvidence: Published 1909 (public domain in the US); Mason died long ago; archive.org marks the scan NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
